name: Bird’s Eye Farm Ina May 5*M (pending) VGVG 83

dam.name: GCH Algedi Farm RB Ocean Flower 6*M *D EEEE 92
Castle Rock Worth Every Penny 3*M *D GVEV 86

copy: Ina has the same powerful, capacious build as her dam Dime Piece (aka Chimi), one of our foundation does. She has wonderful depth of body and her nice wide rump came in handy when her firstborn kid was a breech triplet. She pushed out that kid—our own dear Elena!—with hardly any help.

Ina first freshened in January 2023 with a strong medial and easy-milking open orifices. She easily earned her 5*M designation in 2023, following in some very milky matrilineal hoofsteps. We were thrilled to retain her daughters Elena and Lizzo. She was appraised that June, but six months into her first freshening she didn’t have much udder to show the appraiser! I’ll be keen to see how her mammary appraises when our area is slated for Linear Appraisal again in 2026.

Ina freshened a second time in 2024, and her daughter Elena gave birth the very next day, in the same stall. In a heartwarming show of grandmotherly instinct, Ina helped clean off and nurse her newborn grandkids. (She also ate Elena’s placenta, which—ok?)

Ina then peaked at 4.4 lbs of daily milk and stayed in great condition through a 16 month extended lactation. Her 305 day total was 943 lbs of milk. She finished the lactation with a whopping 1200 lbs of milk and 70 lbs of butterfat.

Ina bears a striking resemblance to her paternal granddam, GCH Algedi Farm RB Ocean Flower 6*M *D EEEE 92. Ocean is a show ring and milk stand legend, and Ina inherited some of her granddam’s grace. Combine that with strength and capacity from her dam Chimi’s genetics and you can see why Ina is such a lovely doe—and stellar producer!

name: Diji Farm Cacao Nib 5*M (pending)
copy: We got the chance to bring in a lovely doeling from Diji Farm in 2022 and young Nib matured beautifully. A friendly snuggler from the start, Nib has the most lovely milk stand manners of the whole herd. When our daughter Laila was five years old she learned to milk with wonderful, patient Nib.

Diji breeds for great conformation, and Nib's line has excellent mammary systems. Lucky for us, Nib inherited a lovely, capacious udder! Her teats are a bit further to the fore than my hands would ideally prefer, but that's being picky. She has great udder texture and hand milks so easily that everybody wants to be on Nib milking assignment. Her dam Skeeter has nice handful teats and Nib seems destined for similar teat length and diameter as she develops.
She's also angular and dairy, qualities we've needed to improve on in our herd. Her grand-sires are both *B Castle Rock hotshots, widening our range of top-notch Castle Rock lines.

Nib's 2024-2025 first lactation was explosive from the start. She peaked at 5 lbs per day (well over half a gallon), and proceeded to marathon it out. Over a *twenty-month* extended lactation, she milked an epic 1600 lbs! Her 305-day total was 1000 lbs. (Okay, it was technically 998, but come on. 😁)

Her first kidding was rough—tangled triplets, the first breech—but that may have been because the kids were a bit too big for dainty Nib. I'm hoping with some prenatal care adjustments she'll have an easier go in 2026. As her midwife I must say the rough birth strengthened our goat-human bond and sure helped build my goat midwifery confidence!
We retained Nib's gorgeous daughter Gianaclis to the herd and expect great things from her as well. We couldn't be more proud of our darling Nib!
<small>Below: Nib's gorgeous dam Skeeter, and Skeeter's spectacular udder. Photos courtesy of Diji Farm</small>

name: Bird’s Eye Farm Elena Ferrante 6*M (pending)

sire.name: Diji Farm Jackson’s Royal Bayliner *B EEE91

dam.name: Diji Farm PU Lil Ms D-Vyne 4*M VEEV90
Bird’s Eye Farm Ina May 5*M (pending) VGVG 83

copy: Elena is gorgeous, sweet and feminine. I’m not sure how this spritely dairy doe emerged from our Chimi/Ina line of deep-bodied power girls! Despite being quite a bit smaller than her dam Ina, Elena gets the job done on the milkstand and in the kidding stall. I love her angularity and front end assembly. Also love that she lets human kids follow her around in the pasture, stopping her for hugs.

Elena freshened in 2024. Of all our does, she is the only one to kid so easily and quietly that we didn’t hear a peep on our turnt-up barn monitor. Having been up the previous night periodically staring at the monitor as she labored in peaceful silence, I awoke to find two clean, fluffy kids on the ground. Now that’s the kind of kidding you want! (Grandma Ina also helped: details on Ina’s page.)

Elena milked 776 lbs of milk, 45 lbs of butterfat in her first 305. We didn’t keep her on extended lactation for her first freshening since she was younger and smaller than our other does were when we put them on long lactations. Then again, her daughter Gilia decided to keep milking for months after that (yes, we let tween goats nurse if they want to) and Elena stayed in great condition. Seems she can indeed handle the long haul!

While her production is very good, Elena has thus far been easier to milk by machine than by hand. Her teats were on the smaller side this first lactation, though that should improve. Her medial suspensory ligament is also not as strong as I’d like.

We were tickled when Elena brought her little chamoisée doeling Gilia into the world and onto the farm. Gilia represents the fourth generation of our herd. And when Elena becomes a grandma in 2026: fifth generation!

name: Bird's Eye Farm Lizabeth Darcy

sire.name: Diji Farm Jackson’s Royal Bayliner *B EEE91

dam.name: Diji Farm PU Lil Ms D-Vyne 4*M VEEV90
Bird’s Eye Farm Ina May 5*M (pending) VGVG 83

copy: We planned to only keep one Ina daughter in 2023, but Lizzo and Elena both looked so great as kids that we couldn't decide! Lizzo was born small, but she was so spunky and determined to nurse that she quickly caught up with her triplet brother and sister. We were charmed by her tenacity and friendly disposition. She's also got a great front end and is very level.

We generally only kid every other year. Lizzo was born in an off year, so we assumed we wouldn't get to breed her or her sister Elena until they were over two years old. As it turned out, we got a chance to have a visiting buck in spring 2024. Elena happened to be in heat that week, so she got bred, but Lizzo did not. This gives us a cool opportunity to see how two genetically identical does do when they're first bred at different ages.

In our experience so far, does bred younger are less likely to get overconditioned, but their first freshening milk production is a bit lower, and they often have fewer kids. Does bred a bit older can build more strength and stay in great condition on extended lactation, even on their first freshening. (They're also likelier to have multiples: Lizzo's granddam Chimi had quads when she first freshened as a two year-old.) Breeding at about 18 months seems like the sweet spot for our farm, but it will be interesting to see what the Elena/Lizzo experiment teaches us.

Lizzo's sister Elena, dam Ina and granddam Chimi have all been great milkers for us, and we're excited to have Liz join the tradition. She has been a very nice auntie to her niece Gilia, so I look forward to finally seeing Liz with her own kids!

name: Bird's Eye Farm Masha Gessen

dam.name: Diji Farm GB Darling Snow 1*M VEEE 91

copy: Masha blends our Bird's Eye Farm line with the excellent breeding tradition of Diji Farm. Her dam Zora and granddam Zadie (aka Ginger Zinger) are extra friendly, beloved members of our herd. They come from excellent lines and have produced well, but their mammaries are not as robust as our Chimi-Ina or Nib lines.

Enter the handsome buck Diji Farm AH Snow's Legacy! Larry (as he's known) was bred from two of Diji's finest. His mom Darling Snow was a milkstand star with a spectacular mammary. Carol of Diji Farm said Snow had such a tabletop line you could have set plates on it. And her Linear Appraisal score of VEEE 91 is extraordinary for a Nigie. Larry's dad is Austin Healey, who sired our own Nib, another milkstand star.

Put that all together and you get lovely, level, long-bodied Masha, who freshens for the first time in 2026. Her conformation is even better than Zora's or Zadie's, and I can't wait to see the udder on this one!

name: Bird's Eye Farm Gianaclis

sire.name: Diji Farm Jackson's Royal Bayliner *B EEE91

dam.name: Diji Farm PU Lil Ms D-Vyne 4*M VEEV90

copy: Our young princess Gianaclis! Giana is the first daughter of our rockstar milker Diji Farms AH Cacao Nib 5*M. Once we'd seen Nib's lovely udder and staggering milk haul (1000 lbs in 305 days) there was no doubt little Giana had a big future. She is built exactly like her mom, dairy and angular but also strong. (When Giana's adorable white patches and Nib's big udder are out of view you can barely tell mother from daughter!) Like her dam and granddam, Giana is very level, with straight front legs and well-angled rear legs.

Giana will be gunning for her 6*M designation with her first freshening in 2026. She's scheduled to freshen the same week as her dam, so Nib can be Giana's milkstand partner and teach her daughter excellent milk stand manners.

We're also big fans of Giana's sire, Diji Farm's own JRB Typhoon aka "Jimmy Leggs." Jimmy previously bred our Ina, and their daughter Elena has grown into a great, productive dairy doe. Jimmy brings primo genetics from both Diji and the legendary Buttin' Heads herd.

And speaking of legends, Giana is named for dairywoman extraordinaire Gianaclis Caldwell, whose books on goat care and cheesemaking—along with her exceptional Oregon herd of Nigerian Dwarf goats at Pholia Farm—have inspired our farm.
The world is yours, Giana!

copy: Dime Piece, better known as Chimi, is a powerful doe with tremendous body capacity, standing 22 inches at the withers. She has a long, level topline, straight front legs and nice rear leg angulation. Chimi has a gleeful appetite for pasture and hay. She doesn’t have the elegant angularity of some dairy does, a quality are working to improve on with her offspring.

Chimi first freshened in 2019 with a soft, well-attached, capacious udder with good teat placement and lovely open orifices, making her a joy to milk. She rocked an epic 570-day extended lactation in 2022-2023, peaking near 4 pounds per day and easily earning her 4*M designation. Filling a half-gallon jar with the day’s milk—from one little Nigie—is quite satisfying!

With both parents from Castle Rock Farm, Chimi has superb dairy genetics. Her dam, Castle Rock Worth Every Penny 3*M *D, produced 740 pounds of milk in 247 days as a yearling first-freshener and 950 pounds in a 305-day second lactation. Her sire’s dam, GCH CRF Castle Rock Roxanne 1*M *D VEEE 91, has quite the mammary reputation, having won Best Udder of Breed fourteen times.
Chimi and her half-sis Zadie are our foundation does, and we feel lucky to have begun our herd with such fine genetics. As the saying goes: "They say she’s a dime; I say she’s underrated."
notes: 1st choice doe retained; 1st choice wether CS

name: Bird’s Eye Farm Zora Neale 1*M (pending)
notes: 1st choice doe retained; 2nd choice doe LF; 1st choice wether CS

dam.name: GCH Algedi Farm RB Ocean Flower 6*M *D EEEE 92

copy: Zora was the first Bird’s Eye Farm-born doe that we retained and we’re so proud of her.

Zora is spritely and feminine. Her dam, Ginger Zinger (aka Zadie) is one of our foundational does. Like her dam, Zora is very level with straight front legs and well-angled rear legs. She’s incredibly friendly and as a kid was always looking for a human lap in which to snuggle. In a herd with many gold coats, Zora stands out rocking her white-flecked-with-chocolate look. She’s not as long-bodied as her aunt Chimi or cousin Ina, but holds her own on the milk stand.
Her dam Zadie has a gorgeous, capacious udder and bestowed such patient maternal love that Zora was teat-fed until she was well over a year old.

Zora has great genetics from both sides. Her Castle Rock lineage is rich with milk stars. And her paternal granddam GCH Algedi Farm RB Ocean Flower 6*M *D EEEE 92 is a show ring and milk stand legend.

Zora freshened in 2022 and milked nearly three pounds per day that summer. She freshens again in 2024 and will be on test to earn her milk star at her second freshening. We hope she may also have a daughter this time!

name: Harley Hillside Ginger Zinger

dam.name: GCH CRF Castle Rock Roxanne 1*M *D VEEE 91
SGCH Castle Rock Breakin My Heart 6*M 6*D VEEE 90

copy: Zadie is a petite, feminine doe who comes from a long line of stellar milkers. She stands 20.5” at the withers and has a level topline, straight front legs and nice rear leg angulation. Zadie has good body capacity and a mighty pretty little face. She’s a serious sweetheart, often going for the cuddles even before the treats. Petite though she is, Zadie is herd queen. When the goats head out to pasture she takes the lead.

Her sire’s dam, GCH CRF Castle Rock Roxanne 1*M *D VEEE 91, is a star in the show ring and on the milkstand, winning Best Udder of Breed no less than fourteen times. Her other granddam, SGCH Castle Rock Breakin My Heart 6*M 6*D VEEE 90, made Top Ten in ADGA’s protein production category in 2016—and gave 1210 pounds of milk that year.

Zadie had such a smooth 2019 kidding that the first babe was on the ground before we could run from house to barn. She easily fed three kids, including her big wether Giannis. And she kept right on patiently feeding the pair we retained for well over a year. (Being curious about extended lactations, we find this a promising trait in terms of sustaining will to milk over a long period.) The long lactation did seem to wear on her, so she’s taking a well-earned break. Her daughter Zora has the same sweet disposition and elegant bearing as her dam and will be next up on our breeding schedule.

Zadie’s first freshening udder was soft with great attachment and capacity, though her teat placement and orifices aren’t as ideal as her half-sister Chimi’s, so she took longer to milk out. Since our primary focus for 2019 was growing our herd, we let her kids hog the milk (as mentioned above), but Zadie was still giving us over a pound of milk each morning; we’d love to get her on milk test when she next freshens.
Along with her half-sister, Chimi, Zadie makes up our foundational pair of does, and we couldn’t have wished for a finer duo to start our herd!
